name: dlmalloc
listed_description: Doug Lea's general-purpose memory allocator, named by the book as an alternative to the default C library malloc and free.
reason: Mirror repo (README: 'This isn't my code, but I like to use it'; files malloc.c, malloc.h, Makefile, CMakeLists.txt, 8 commits) has no benchmarks. malloc.c header only says it is 'among the fastest' with no numbers. Doug Lea's page gee.cs.oswego.edu/dl/html/malloc.html is unreachable (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). Two WebSearch queries found no dlmalloc-versus-glibc number; glibc ptmalloc2 is itself derived from dlmalloc, and mimalloc-bench and f18m/malloc-benchmarks do not include dlmalloc. Directional claim only.

name: hardened_malloc (GrapheneOS)
listed_description: Actively developed security-focused drop-in malloc for Android Bionic, musl and glibc, based on the OpenBSD malloc design.
reason: MIT, 2.0k stars, last commit 2026-10-18. README states it aims for 'decent overall performance with a focus on long-term performance and memory usage rather than allocator micro-benchmarks' and 'much less metadata overhead and memory waste from fragmentation than a more traditional allocator design', with no timings and no named baseline numbers; only its own size-class waste table. No benchmark directory (test/ and androidtest/ are functional tests). mimalloc-bench includes it as 'hm' but its README gives no hm numbers, and one WebSearch for a hardened_malloc versus glibc slowdown found none. Directional claim only.
